title: ADR-02 Recorder, witness, verify and PII side store
outcome: Hash-chained C2 record written only by the gateway, a separate witness process taking a signed (seq, head, tick) every tick, ks verify, and a redactable side store for values; due 24 Nov
acceptance: ADR file ≤900 words with sections Context, Decision, Consequences, Interface touched (which of C1–C6), Tests that prove it
verify checks chain, agent+gateway signatures, witness heads, seq gaps and reconciliation (state = fold(log)), prints first bad index, exits non-zero
Log holds hashes only, values live in the side store; witness-head stall raises an alert; claim limited to 'tamper-evident up to the last witnessed head' (no Merkle)
Tests listed map to RT7 (line edit), RT8 (full rewrite) and a tail-truncation case
summary: Freeze applied (<=1,300 words): RunAnchor/--head, count chain, strict-parse split (TAMPER parse_error), truncation first_bad n+1, freeze trigger from chained ks.alert, F4 dispatch-window check, F6 TTI from chained alerts, witness topology/stall, RT8(g,h). Amendments (Call #2) listed.
review:
[kabir · changes] Verdict: CHANGES. The structure is right and the acceptance criteria are met on paper: 897 words, all five sections; verify checks chain, both signatures, witness heads, seq gaps and reconciliation, prints first_bad and exits non-zero; values live in the side store; there is a stall alert; the claim stays "tamper-evident up to the last witnessed head" with no Merkle trees; tests map to RT7, RT8 and tail truncation. A jury can still beat verify, though, and several pass criteria contradict the decision text. PMO has already decided `count` (contracts v1.1).

MUST-FIX
M1 Keyring swap defeats verify (SEC-03 B1). keys.json is an editable run-dir file, and verify takes every public key from it. An insider who holds no key rewrites the chain, generates their own gateway and witness keypairs, rewrites keys.json, and re-signs every record and checkpoint, and verify returns OK. That is RT8 without the witness key, which the THREAT-MODEL says is detected. Fix: the console prints keyring_hash and config_hash at start, and at the end prints a RunAnchor {seq, head, tick, count, keyring_hash, config_hash} (CON-02). `ks verify --head` takes that anchor line and checks the hashes before any signature. VerifyReport gains `anchored`. The C1 claim holds only for anchored verification; unanchored it is "consistent, not anchored". ADR-07's `ks verify RUN [--json]` has no --head flag, so add it there too. SPEC RT8 gains variant (h), a keyring swap: WITNESS when anchored, documented as outside the claim when unanchored.
M2 count (PMO decision). Delete the "Contract gap … Fallback" paragraph. Specify: count starts at 1 and goes +1 per checkpoint line; verify checks w[i].count == i. The anchor's count must equal the last line's count, and its head must equal that line's head. Checkpoints: tick strictly increasing, seq non-decreasing (no-op ticks repeat seq/head, per ADR-00), seq <= n.
M3 Strict parse sends tamper to IO. Step 1 maps every parse failure to Exit.IO. (a) A tampered side entry fails SideEntry validation at parse (checked: ValidationError), so RT7(b) yields IO, not TAMPER. (b) A juror who edits record.jsonl in an editor and types an uppercase hex digit, adds a space or adds a blank line fails strict parse, so the LIVE RT7 beat prints IO with no first_bad. (c) RunDir.validate requires witness.jsonl, so RT8(f) "deleted witness.jsonl" is IO before your "fails closed with WITNESS" rule can run. Fix: Exit.IO only when config.json, keys.json or record.jsonl is missing or unreadable. A record line that fails to parse or validate gives TAMPER, first_bad = that line's number, reason parse_error. A witness line that fails gives WITNESS. A missing or empty witness.jsonl gives WITNESS, first_bad = 1. A side entry is parsed without its validator and re-hashed; a mismatch gives TAMPER, first_bad = the lowest seq that references the hash, reason side_entry_mismatch. Put the side-store pass in the ordered list (after the record pass, before the witness pass).
M4 Truncation first_bad. The decision gives first_bad = checkpoint.seq for a checkpoint with seq > n, while test (d) expects last_kept_seq + 1. Checkpoints cover several records each, so the two differ. Fix: a checkpoint with seq > n gives WITNESS, first_bad = n + 1, reason truncated. An anchor mismatch gives WITNESS, reason head_mismatch, first_bad = min(anchor.seq, n) + 1. Test (d) must truncate below the last checkpoint; otherwise the cut is past the claim boundary and OK is correct.
M5 The tamper freeze has no trigger. Nothing specifies who runs verify on a live run or how often, and an edit made after the run leaves no tamper alert in alerts.jsonl. So `ks recover --dry-run` on the RT7 copy cannot return FROZEN as your test requires. Fix: (a) `ks recover` (including --dry-run) runs verify first and exits FROZEN on any non-OK result. (b) Live: each tick, the monitor re-reads record.jsonl and compares it with the gateway's in-memory running head; a mismatch raises tamper. (c) The freeze is derived from records (SEC-03 F6: alerts submitted as chained ks.alert envelopes), never from the unsigned alerts.jsonl alone. (d) Say what ends a freeze. I propose nothing does: it lasts until run end.
M6 Witness topology and key. (a) "It reads the record read-only" contradicts ADR-00, where the gateway sends (seq, head, tick), and record.jsonl is gateway-only. Pick ADR-00's version. The witness signs what it is sent; it adds anchoring, not re-verification. (b) "Own in-memory key": ADR-00 has the gateway derive the witness key and send it over. In fresh mode the witness must generate its own key and send only the public key (Panel ADR-00 M6e). Without that, "insider holds no witness key" rests on the gateway alone. (c) Name the head store path `<run>/witness-heads/` (0700, witness uid; RunDir layout, CON-02), and file modes per SEC-03 F1 (witness.jsonl created and owned by the witness uid).
M7 Stall semantics. ADR-02 uses "W ticks"; ADR-00 has the tick wait for the ack. Adopt the Panel's ADR-00 M4d: wait up to the deadline, then proceed and raise witness_stall. W is a named constant (1 under that rule). Settle hard: ADR-02 says never hard; ADR-04 and HARD_ALLOWED say yes, with a recovery freeze (SEC-03 N4). I propose hard=false, with the freeze tied to the kind.
M8 RT8(g) is vacuous. ADR-00 takes a final checkpoint at run end, so a completed run has no unwitnessed tail and g tests nothing. Fix: g uses a run dir snapshotted between flush and checkpoint (hook `GatewayHooks.skip_checkpoint` at tick k), and the anchor test shows the same edit is caught once the final anchor exists.

SHOULD-FIX
- Reconcile is exact only if every state change is a record. Outbox status changes and dispatch (SEC-03 F4, ADR-03) and recovery writes must carry write_sets, or every clean run fails RECONCILE. Add that dependency and a clean-run test (verify OK including reconcile). Default --state: <run>/workspace/state.db if present; otherwise skip and report reason no_state, ok=true, so no silent pass.
- Add per-record checks to verify: an exec ks.control/ks.recover.* record must be by a system principal, with issued_by == envelope.agent_id and conn_id c-0 (F2); epochs fold monotonically (B3); expiry_tick >= tick on exec/hold (F3); ts_us formula (N5).
- More reasons: witness_sig_invalid, witness_missing, count_mismatch, truncated, parse_error, side_entry_mismatch, agent_sig_mismatch, keyring_mismatch.
- Add the header line (Owner, Reviewer, Binding); fix the typo "0600,.".
Re-review needs: M1-M8 in the text, and tests (b), (d), (f) and (g) rewritten to match. Contract asks are in CON-02-requests.md.

[kabir · done] M1 RunAnchor + keyring_hash/config_hash checked before signatures, anchored flag, RT8(h): resolved (ADR-07 --head flag is ADR-07's item). M2 count from 1 with chain, anchor count/head match, tick/seq monotonic rules, fallback paragraph deleted: resolved. M3 IO only for missing config/keys/record; parse_error and side_entry_mismatch are TAMPER; missing witness is WITNESS witness_missing first_bad=1; side pass ordered after record pass: resolved. M4 truncated first_bad=n+1, head_mismatch first_bad=min(anchor.seq,n)+1, test (d) truncates below last checkpoint: resolved. M5 recover runs verify first, live monitor head compare, freeze from chained ks.alert records, lasts to run end: resolved. M6 gateway sends (seq,head,tick), witness own key in fresh mode, witness-heads 0700 and file modes: resolved. M7 wait to deadline then alert, W=1, witness_stall/tamper never hard with freeze by kind: resolved. M8 RT8(g) via GatewayHooks.skip_checkpoint, caught once anchor exists: resolved. Should-fixes (write_sets for dispatch/recovery, no_state skip, per-record checks, reasons, header) also applied. Nit: record.jsonl is 0640 group=witness gid, which sits oddly with ADR-00 gateway-only record; not a hole since the witness signs only what it is sent.
